title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 200 (Ratification of unauthorized act cannot injure third person)

content.overview: An act done by one person on behalf of another, without such other person’s authority, which, if done with authority, would have the effect of subjecting a third person to damages, or of terminating any right or interest of a third person, cannot, by ratification, be made to have such effect.
content.glance: Ratification cannot make an unauthorized act operate to subject a third person to damages or to terminate a third person’s right or interest.
content.study: An act done by one person on behalf of another, without such other person’s authority, which, if done with authority, would have the effect of subjecting a third person to damages, or of terminating any right or interest of a third person, cannot, by ratification, be made to have such effect. Illustrations: unauthorized demand for delivery cannot be ratified to make the holder liable in damages; unauthorized notice terminating a lease cannot be ratified to bind the lessee.

sections.heading: Unauthorized act
sections.body: Act done on behalf of another without authority.

sections.heading: Would injure third person if authorized
sections.body: If authorized, would subject third person to damages or terminate third person’s right or interest.

sections.heading: No ratification to that effect
sections.body: Cannot by ratification be made to have such effect.

provisions.title: Ratification of unauthorized act cannot injure third person

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 200 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify unauthorized act; test whether authorization would injure a third person; deny ratification to that prejudicial effect.
